name: Qiwu’s reported steelmaking
summary: A Chinese biography says the sixth-century smith Qiwu made sabre steel by heating powdered cast iron with soft-iron blanks for days, an early described steelmaking recipe.
description: A biography describes heating powdered cast iron with soft-iron blanks for several days to make steel for sabres.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

impact.note: One textual report of a better sabre-steel recipe within a continuing Chinese co-fusion practice; scores imply tier 3, below the reviewed tier 2.

date.label: 6th century CE
date.basis: Practice assigned retrospectively to Qiwu Huaiwen in Beishi, chapter 89; this is the reported sixth-century activity, not the later compilation date.
